content.thinking: In SCOPe 2.08, I found PA1492 (1t1j) and nucleoside 2-deoxyribosyltransferase (1f8y) share the same fold and superfamily (c.23.14) but sit in different families, indicating a common evolutionary origin without implying shared function. I couldn't verify SCOP 1.69's classification via the tool (it only covers SCOPe releases), so that part relies on my recollection of Andreeva et al. 2008 and should be confirmed against the original source.

answers.answer: In SCOPe 2.08 (current), PA1492 (1t1j; d1t1ja1/d1t1jb1, c.23.14.2, family 'Hypothetical protein PA1492', Pseudomonas aeruginosa) and nucleoside 2-deoxyribosyltransferase (1f8y; d1f8ya_/d1f8yb_, c.23.14.1, family 'N-deoxyribosyltransferase', Lactobacillus leichmannii) share class c (a/b), fold c.23 (Flavodoxin-like) and superfamily c.23.14 (N-(deoxy)ribosyltransferase-like, sunid 52309), but sit in different families (sunid 110461 vs 52310). So they are now classified as remote homologs (same superfamily, different families). In SCOP 1.69, as I recall from Andreeva et al. 2008 (this part was NOT verified with the tools, which only serve SCOPe), PA1492 was not placed with the nucleoside 2-deoxyribosyltransferases (a structural-genomics unknown-function protein with no superfamily-level link; I am not certain whether it was a separate fold or a different superfamily). Later structural/sequence comparison led to moving it into c.23.14 as its own family. Caveats: superfamily membership supports common ancestry but not close relationship; function must not be transferred from 1f8y to 1t1j (PA1492 remains annotated hypothetical); sharing a fold alone would not imply homology, here the homology claim comes from the superfamily assignment; the 1.69 details should be checked against the paper or the archived SCOP 1.69.
evidence_used: pretrained knowledge of Andreeva et al. 2008
